text:
nate: hi team, day 2 for me. trying to get node + yarn via asdf on my M1 but keep hitting node-gyp build errors for native modules. here's what i ran:
``
brew install pkg-config python@3.10 openssl@1.1
export PATH="$(brew --prefix python@3.10)/bin:$PATH"
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
```
but `npm rebuild` still fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_NODE` and `node-gyp: make failed`. any quick tips or a checklist so i don't miss obvious mac arm quirks?

emma: welcome! two quick things: 1) make sure you installed the nodejs plugin dependencies per asdf-nodejs docs (gpg keys etc). run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. 2) if you have multiple python installs, `node-gyp` sometimes picks the wrong one. `which python3` inside the same shell as asdf matters.

sam: also check you don't have an intel brew at /usr/local. `brew --prefix` should be /opt/homebrew. if you previously ran homebrew under rosetta terminal, uninstall that one. another helpful step: open a new terminal launched with iTerm's native arch (not rosetta) and run `arch` to verify `arm64`.

nate: thanks. what about dotfiles? i pulled dotfiles from the repo and one of the scripts adds `/usr/local/bin` to PATH which seems wrong on my mac. safe edit or is there a canonical company dotfile i should use?

emma: we have a minimal dotfile in the onboarding repo meant for mac arm: `dotfiles/minimal/macos-arm.sh`. prefer that. if you forked personal dotfiles, remove hardcoded /usr/local references. put machine-specific tweaks in `~/.localrc` and source it from .zshrc so upstream changes don't clobber you.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: do not commit secrets or machine-specific paths. Use `.env.local` and add to .gitignore. See onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/docs/onboarding/checklist

sam: for the node-gyp specific error, run `npm i --build-from-source --verbose` and paste logs if it still fails. often the missing piece is `xcode-select --install` or `npm config set python $(which python3)`. also `export npm_config_loglevel=verbose` helps debug.

nate: ok i'll try the minimal dotfile + python path + reinstall node. one last thing: ssh-agent forwarding in devcontainer; i tried `forwardAgent: true` in devcontainer.json but my container can't reach github. any gotchas?

emma: make sure ssh-agent is actually running on host and you added the key: `ssh-add -l`. for mac with the new ssh, you might need `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain` then `ssh-add -K` to persist. in devcontainer, add `mounts`: `- source=/Users/nate/.ssh-agent.sock,target=/ssh-agent,type=bind` and set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent` in container env. we have a small script in onboarding repo `scripts/devcontainer-ssh-setup.sh` that helps.

nate: perfect, thanks. i'll reply here with logs if anything else breaks. appreciate the quick pointers :bow:
